title: PERHAPS THE LORD WILL ACT.
paragraphs:
Two words that don’t sound like certainty.
Two words that don’t look like victory.

Not with thunder.
Not with guarantees.
But with a trembling step forward.

Saul was sitting under a pomegranate tree.
Six hundred soldiers.
Swords scarce.
Fear everywhere.
Across the valley stood the Philistine outpost—armed, trained, waiting.
Then Jonathan looked at his armor-bearer and whispered:

“Come, let’s go over to the outpost of those uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act for us. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”
—1 Samuel 14:6
Here’s the scandal of faith most people miss.

Jonathan had no army.
No strategy briefing.
No prophetic confirmation.
Just a conviction about who God is.
Because when you know God’s character, you can move even when you don’t know God’s plan.

Sharp cliffs.
Hands scraping rock.
Enemy soldiers watching from above.
“Come up here, and we’ll teach you a lesson.”
Then something only God could do happened.
What began with two men became a divine rout.
Faith is moving because you know God is able, even when you don’t know if He will act the way you hope.
Jonathan’s faith did not demand a miracle.
It trusted God enough to risk obedience.
Some of you are standing at your own cliff today.

A calling that terrifies you.
A ministry that feels impossible.
A battle against sin that looks unwinnable.
But sometimes heaven whispers only one word:
Because the power was never in Jonathan.
The power was in the Lord who saves “by many or by few.”
But the greatest battle was still ahead.
Centuries later, another Son of Israel walked toward a hill.
At the cross, Jesus faced a far greater enemy—sin, death, and hell itself.
And where we deserved defeat, He secured victory.
Three days later the stone rolled away.
So today you can move with courage.
But because the God who raised Jesus from the dead is still able to act.
Even if your prayer begins with a trembling whisper:
🔥 We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
